title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes, Grothendieck is building an algebraic, axiomatic framework for a tame ('modérée') topology. It is organised around three 'ateliers' (workshops, i.e. universes of objects): 𝔉, the figures; 𝔐, the strata or irreducible pieces; and ℒ, a third, more geometric universe. On 𝔉 he has several relations: inclusion ≤; a 'strong' relation ≪; a refinement relation ≼ (≾); and the derived symmetric relations of compatibility (≬) and disjunction (∥) from page 9.

Axioms paragraph. One can axiomatise starting from any of the three ateliers. The axioms are formally simplest on 𝔉 and most sophisticated on ℒ. Their intuitive content runs the opposite way: least transparent if one stays inside 𝔉, most transparent in ℒ. He asks whether 𝔐 behaves the same way.

(1.16) Three alternative choices of primitive structure on 𝔉:
(a) (≤, ≪);
(b) (≤, ≼);
(c) ≪ together with the 'déploiement' map 𝔉 → P(…), F ↦ F̃.
A marginal addition dated 20 June, apparently revising alternative (b), reports a new geometric characterisation (or procedure) for ≪. Not fully legible; the details are not given here.

The déploiement F ↦ F̃ is equivalent to the incidence relation 'F is a stratum of G' (F ∈ 𝔐 and F ≤ G). This is formalised as (1.17): F ◁ G :⇔ F ≤ G and F ∈ 𝔐.

The next page lists the six relations (◁, ≤, ≼, ≪, ∥, ≬). It then shows that ◁ and ≤ determine each other:
- 𝔐 is the set of completely join-prime ('strictly irreducible') elements of (𝔉, ≤);
- F̃ = {X ∈ 𝔐 : X ◁ F};
- F ≤ G ⇔ F̃ ⊂ G̃.
This is Birkhoff-type representation of a distributive lattice by the down-sets of its poset of join-primes. The figure lattice is recovered as a lattice of subsets of the stratum poset, much like recovering a finite stratified (Alexandrov) space from its face poset.

Purpose: find a minimal, intrinsic set of combinatorial data from which the whole 'algèbre des figures' (and the atlas, cf. p. 9) can be reconstructed. This would found a stratified, tame topology axiomatically.
errors: Calling ◁ an order relation is loose: F ◁ F holds only for F ∈ 𝔐, so ◁ is reflexive only on 𝔐. Grothendieck flags this himself in the margin of p. 11.

Recovering ≤ from ◁ via F ≤ G ⇔ F̃ ⊂ G̃ needs an unstated hypothesis: every figure is the sup of the strata below it, i.e. the lattice is 'spatial' or has enough join-primes. This presumably comes from the axioms, but it is not stated on this page.
Alternative (c) lists ≪ without ≤. That works only because ≤ is recoverable from the déploiement (as shown on p. 11); this is not argued here.

ideas.what: Three equivalent axiomatic starting points (figures 𝔉, strata 𝔐, a geometric universe ℒ), with a trade-off between formal simplicity and intuitive transparency.
ideas.modern_name: Alternative axiomatisations of tame/stratified topology (cf. o-minimal structures, stratified spaces via posets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tame topology programme: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984); o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 only calls for a 'topologie modérée'; this axiomatic scheme is not there.

ideas.what: Incidence relation F ◁ G (F is a stratum of G) and the déploiement F̃ (the set of strata of F).
ideas.modern_name: Face/incidence poset of a stratification; Alexandrov topology on the stratum poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Alexandrov, combinatorial topology); exit-path/poset-stratified viewpoint: MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka

ideas.what: Equivalence of the data ≤ and ◁ via strictly join-irreducible (join-prime) elements and the embedding F ↦ F̃.
ideas.modern_name: Birkhoff representation theorem / spatial distributive lattices (frames–locales duality)

ideas.what: Choice of primitive relations (≤, ≪), (≤, ≼), or (≪, F ↦ F̃) on the figure lattice.

missed.claim: A programme to axiomatise tame topology lattice-theoretically through three interchangeable 'ateliers' (𝔉, 𝔐, ℒ). The six fundamental relations (◁, ≤, ≼, ≪, ∥, ≬) and three choices of primitive structure are never worked out in print. The dated 20 June note announcing a geometric characterisation of ≪ (or a new procedure for it) is a thread to follow in the subsequent pages.
missed.quote: On peut prendre pour axiomes de base des axiomatiques des ateliers, soit 𝔉, soit 𝔐, soit ℒ … (20 juin) Non, je viens de trouver une caractérisation géométrique pour ≪
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Recent work treats stratified spaces through their stratum posets (exit-path ∞-categories, conically smooth stratifications), and model-theoretic tame geometry is axiomatic. Grothendieck's purely order-theoretic, point-free axiomatics of figures and strata, with compatibility and refinement as primitives, is a third route. It is not represented in either literature.

missed.claim: Implicitly links tame topology to Birkhoff/Stone-type duality: figures form a spatial distributive lattice whose join-primes are the strata. This is a point-free (locale-like) foundation for tame topology.
missed.quote: i.e. la relation d'incidence "F est une strate de G" (i.e. F∈𝔐 et F≤G)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Point-free or 'spectral' presentations of o-minimal sites (cf. Edmundo–Prelli, real spectra in Coste–Roy) exist, but are not phrased via strata as join-primes plus a refinement relation.

deep.surprise_reason: The individual mathematics is routine: Birkhoff duality and incidence posets. The interest is in seeing Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic architecture for 'topologie modérée' (ateliers, six relations, choice of primitives). Only Esquisse-level hints of it are known.
transcription_corrections: 'quand on part plus ou moins dans 𝔉' is more likely 'quand on reste plus ou moins dans 𝔉'.
'(en peut-il être pareil pour 𝔐 ?)' is likely '(en est-il pareil pour 𝔐 ?)'.
'les axiomes intuitifs' could also read 'axiomes naturels'; the word is uncertain.
The 20 June marginal note is uncertain. It reads roughly '(20 juin) Non, … un nouveau procédé … géométrique plus ≪'; 'caractérisation géométrique' is a conjecture.
In 'déploiement de F vu comme partie de …', the target set should be 𝔐 (since F̃ ⊂ 𝔐, cf. (1.22)), not 𝔉. The hand appears to write 𝔉, which may be a slip.
In (1.16)c the struck symbol is ≼; read 'c) ≪ et 𝔉 → P(…)'.
Opening fragment 'ci inspirant' continues from the previous page ('…les raisons qui aux ci inspirant'), probably '…qui m'y ont inspiré' or similar.
